  "conclusion":"Caring responsiveness to the most acute life-threatening need provisionally supports giving the blanket to Rowan, though the moral cost of breaking Ellis’s promise to Sasha remains a live concern.",
  "strongest_objection":"Breaking Ellis’s explicit promise to Sasha undermines trust and may inflict relational harm that care ethics takes seriously.",
  "answer_to_objection":"The care duty to address the gravest vulnerability (80% chance to save Rowan versus 60% for Sasha) is, in this context, more urgent than fulfilling the earlier assurance; responsiveness to life-or-death need can override but does not erase the wrong of breaking a promise.",
  "reversal_condition":"If the survival probabilities were roughly equal, or Sasha’s need became at least as urgent as Rowan’s, the relational promise could tip the balance toward giving the blanket to Sasha.",
